goal: enumerate the entire set of log/log_fn call lines whose arguments mention 'panel', partitioning so that every CodeIntel page is untruncated, then prove the union against the same-file rg population
population_definition: lines where a log( or log_fn( call opens and the same line's arguments contain 'panel' (case-insensitive)

partitions.note: this partition is the only one that is a superset of its population slice: the alternation names event tokens without also requiring 'panel', so 5 rows whose args never say panel come back with it (see extra_rows)
these are the rows with no uppercase event token - lowercase prose-style panel ops (setFocusable, setAlwaysOnTop, WS_EX_*), which the earlier event-word regex could never reach

union_analysis.partition_overlaps: none - the 7 CodeIntel line sets are pairwise disjoint, so union = sum = 92
extra_row_identity: 3837 log(f'OUTSIDE_CLICK_HOOK uninstalled reason=...') - no 'panel' in args
union_analysis.extra_row_explanation: P6's alternation matches the event token but does not also require 'panel' inside the argument list, so it also catches same-event lines that never mention panel. They are correctly outside the population and are reported rather than silently dropped.
union_analysis.every_partition_parity: set_equal=true for all 7 (CodeIntel line set identical to the same-regex rg line set)

proof.rg_multiline_positive_control: rg -U -n -P -- '(?i)\b(?:log|log_fn)\s*\([^)]*panel' finds match starts at 87 single-line rows plus 6983/6984 and 9028/9029
proof.conclusion: the patterns were accepted (no regex error) but matched nothing, while rg -U proves both strings exist across the line break, so the CodeIntel grep engine is line-oriented and cannot match a call whose panel argument sits on a continuation line

multiline.corrected_true_population: 87 observable call sites + 2 multiline-only call sites = 89 call sites whose arguments mention panel; only the 87 are recoverable through codeintel_grep

verdict.status: exhaustive for everything CodeIntel can see
